title: Show battery percentage on the Bluetooth widget icon when there's a single connected bluetooth device
line: The Bluetooth tray icon can now show the battery percentage of the connected device, turned on from its right-click menu.
explanation: Nothing was broken: the Bluetooth widget's icon could only carry a badge with the number of connected devices, so a headset's battery level was visible only in the tooltip and popup. A new opt-in option (off by default, next to the existing count badge toggle in the right-click menu) fills the same badge with the percentage, e.g. "70%", when exactly one connected device reports a battery, as comment 1 asks for devices without a battery. With two or more battery devices it falls back to the count badge if that is enabled.

commits.message:
applet: add option to show battery percentage on the icon

The tray icon could only show the number of connected devices, so the
battery level of headphones was only visible in the tooltip or popup. A
new option fills the badge with the percentage when one device has one.

BUG: 528165

media.caption: Master: the widget's right-click menu only offers the badge with the number of connected devices
With the change: new item "Show badge with battery percentage of the connected device"
Master with a connected headset at 70%: the tray icon shows no percentage
With the option on: the tray icon shows a 70% badge

review.text: Solid, idiomatic implementation of the wishlist item: adds an opt-in checkable action matching the existing device-count badge toggle, wires it cleanly into both the context menu and standalone toolbar menu, and counts only connected devices that report a battery (as requested in comment 1) while falling back to the count badge when multiple battery devices are connected. Live updates, i18n formatting, regressions, and autotests are all verified.
